newsitem.title: TURKEY: INFLATION-INDEXED AUCTION BOOSTS TURK BOND DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: INFLATION-INDEXED AUCTION BOOSTS TURK BOND DEMAND.

text.p: The Turkish treasury's announcement of a two-year inflation-indexed bond auction boosted demand for outstanding government papers on the secondary market, bankers said on Monday.
Bankers said they expect higher risk premium at Tuesday's auction due to increased political uncertainities, aggravated by the coalition government's move to call for snap elections.
"The auction will push up overall interest rates in the economy," said a private bank dealer.
The treasury had sold 55.27 trillion lira of two-year bonds at a 29.95 percent risk premium at its latest auction on May 13.
Bankers say demand for two-year bonds will remain low in Tuesday's auction to be held with Wednesday value when the Treasury faces 288.2 trillion lira of bond redemption.
Bankers were expecting the treasury to hold a t-bill auction with a six or nine-month maturity.

The central bank is expected to drain excess cash through open market operations and foreign currency sales later this week if the treasury fails to roll-over its redemption via the two-year bond auction.
